headline: Test 1: Portugal, 1441–1486 · 33:31

items.title: 33:31 · A fleet of six caravels commanded by
items.detail: A fleet of six caravels commanded by Lancarote de Freitas sailed south to the islands of Arguin Bay off the Mauritanian coast, attacked coastal settlements, and packed 235 kidnapped men, women, and children into the holds.

items.title: 33:45 · On August 8 1444 Lancarote s fleet
items.detail: On August 8, 1444, Lancarote's fleet landed those 235 captives on the field outside Lagos in southern Portugal.

items.title: 33:52 · The captives were divided into five lots
items.detail: The captives were divided into five lots on the beach, separating parents from children and husbands from wives while townspeople gathered to watch the spectacle.

items.title: 34:02 · Prince Henry the Navigator attended the Lagos
items.detail: Prince Henry the Navigator attended the Lagos division mounted on a powerful horse, collected his royal quinto, one-fifth of the human cargo, as fiscal sovereign, and knighted Lancarote de Freitas on the spot for the profitability of the voyage.

items.title: 34:18 · Immediately after 1444 Portuguese raiders pushing south
items.detail: Immediately after 1444, Portuguese raiders pushing south past the Senegal River encountered the organized military resistance of Wolof and Mandinka states.
